clue.text: Flag-waver ready to capture a threesome

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it, so one word is put around the other

parts.note: to have something pat is to have it ready and memorised
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Someone waving a flag is all set to take three people prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot shows love of country, and waving the national flag is the stock image of that devotion.

clue.text: Father's a wise man, in a way

parts.note: pa is father, keeping the possessive s
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Dad is in a sense a wise man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' looks like a hedge; way is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way through, a route or corridor.

clue.text: Fix me a label in a hat

indicators.note: these words go inside the hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
taken as written
a tab is a small label

explanation.surface: A request to stick a label inside one's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is dated British slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To timetable an event is to schedule it, to fix its time.

clue.text: Furious buccaneer loses his head

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: a buccaneer is a pirate, a sea robber of the Caribbean

explanation.surface: An angry pirate is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym for angry.

clue.text: Lorry perhaps found in entrance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a vehicle, a means of conveyance; a lorry is a truck
second meaning: the verb to enrapture, delight

explanation.surface: A truck is discovered parked in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance is the verb (en-TRANCE), not the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vehicles and conveyance, and also to carry away with emotion.

clue.text: Turn us against brother, needing it to be in private

indicators.note: turning the little word us around makes it read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
bro is informal for brother
it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Someone is setting siblings against each other, and wants the scheming kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB ROSA is Latin, literally 'under the rose', a symbol of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in English to mean confidentially or secretly.

clue.text: Jockey's garments found in Sunday school

parts.note: a school is a kind or class, as is an ilk; the plural is taken here

explanation.surface: Racing colours turn up at a church class.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter takes school as ilk, a sort or class; the final S makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Silks are the coloured shirts and caps a jockey wears to identify the owner.

clue.text: It's unimportant that Belle is holding a return ticket

definitions.note: a description standing for a trifle, a noun

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the rest goes inside

parts.note: the name is taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: return means the word is reversed

parts.note: a tag is a ticket or label

explanation.surface: Belle shrugs off having a return ticket as no big deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, something of little value.

clue.text: Rotter decapitated an animal

indicators.note: losing the head drops the first letter

parts.note: the word rotter is taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel beheaded an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating aquatic mammal.

clue.text: Cut in card game

parts.note: a can mean per or in, as in twice a day
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone cuts the deck during a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Abridged would be the strict participle; here the word is read as the shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it.

clue.text: Samantha gets degree in dance

parts.note: Sam is the usual short form of Samantha
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Samantha graduates and celebrates by dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance.

clue.text: Pear thrown at gorilla

definitions.note: short for alligator pear, the avocado

indicators.note: letters thrown about land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a piece of fruit at a gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: The alligator pear is an old name for the avocado, after its rough green skin, so the word stands in for the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocados were once commonly called alligator pears for their knobbly, reptilian skin.

clue.text: One caught by the hair, like Bernhardt and Langtry

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase: performers of their kind

parts.note: a means one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is grabbed by the hair, as might befall a famous stage star.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Bernhardt was a French stage star and Lillie Langtry a British one, both of the late 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Both women were celebrated stage performers, so the answer names the profession they shared.

clue.text: Confined queen held inside, worn out

indicators.note: one letter is held within the other word

parts.note: tied means bound or confined

explanation.surface: A queen kept captive is exhausted by her confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for queen from the Latin regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired and worn out are synonyms for exhausted.

clue.text: To shove from below

indicators.note: the answer is made from the word below, its letters reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to push something upwards from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' looks like a direction for the shove; it is the fodder and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push or jostle them aside.

clue.text: State of Victoria post-1861?

parts.note: reads as the Australian state, but means the condition of Queen Victoria
Prince Albert died in 1861, leaving the queen to mourn for forty years

explanation.surface: A question about the Australian state after 1861.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria wore mourning from Albert's death in 1861 until her own in 1901.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of a woman whose husband has died, as the queen's was.

clue.text: Awkwardly sit with a cello and hesitate

indicators.note: awkwardly arranged letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cellist sits clumsily with the instrument and pauses before playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to waver between options, a kind of indecision.

clue.text: Failed to expire in the cold

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as the word cold
to lapse is to expire, as a licence does

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed and died out in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme that collapsed is one that failed.

clue.text: Humiliation for one reaching place for bargains

parts.note: the bargain basement is a store's cut-price floor

explanation.surface: Being reduced to the cheap floor of the department store is shaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is degradation, being humbled or lowered in esteem.

clue.text: Unreliable one has to kiss all but Dorothy and Albert

indicators.note: all but a word means the whole word except its last letter

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
Dot is a short form of Dorothy
Al is a short form of Albert

explanation.surface: Some untrustworthy person has to kiss nearly everyone except Dorothy and Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on stories rather than proof, so it is untrustworthy.

clue.text: Don't vote for a black mark

parts.note: taken as written
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: A voter avoids putting a black mark on the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to cast a vote.

clue.text: Precise demand

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to insist on or require

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means accurate; as a verb, to extract payment or obedience by insistence.

clue.text: Taught first of travellers to take winding detour

indicators.note: the first of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

indicators.note: a winding route twists the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The lead traveller was shown the way on a twisting diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutored means taught privately.

clue.text: Used for bedding, having lumps on retirement

definitions.note: a description standing for the thing used as animal bedding

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: warts are small hard lumps on the skin

explanation.surface: An old mattress gets lumpy once its owner stops working.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried stalks of cereal are the traditional bedding material for livestock.

clue.text: Newly equip last 1,000

parts.note: the rear is the last part

explanation.surface: Supplying the final thousand troops afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply with weapons again.

clue.text: A puzzle designed, we hear, to cause confusion

parts.note: taken as written
a maze is a puzzle of paths

indicators.note: what we hear is how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: meant is intended or designed

explanation.surface: A puzzle was built specifically to baffle people.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is a state of astonished bewilderment.

clue.text: Don't stop when in some pain

indicators.note: one word placed in the other

parts.note: any can mean some
go, keep moving

explanation.surface: Advice to keep going while hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: agony is extreme suffering, the worst degree of physical or mental hurt.

clue.text: Derby course record, with nearly a few more

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, missing its last letter

parts.note: some, as in would you like some more

explanation.surface: A horse-racing record broken by almost a few more.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race run at Epsom Downs in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs racecourse hosts the Derby every summer.

clue.text: Like sign in a mixed sauna

indicators.note: the sign goes inside the reshuffled letters
mixed letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
a logo is a sign or emblem

explanation.surface: A notice hangs in a sauna used by both men and women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed sauna' reads as a unisex sauna; mixed is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous means similar or comparable.

clue.text: Some of the flowers we arranged to maintain

indicators.note: only some of the letters in these words are used, a run of them

parts.note: the letters run across flowers, we and arranged

explanation.surface: Part of the flower display we put together is meant to keep them fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to assert or insist, as to maintain a claim.

clue.text: Time for saintly feasting: any mead drunk?

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A celebrant at a saint's feast asks if there is any mead going.
explanation.definitionFit: A name day is the feast day of the saint one is named after.

clue.text: Thomas, when in action, comes back downgraded

indicators.note: coming back means the word reads in reverse
one name goes inside the other word

parts.note: a deed is an action
Tom is a short form of Thomas

explanation.surface: Thomas returns from active service having lost rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoted means reduced to a lower rank or position.
